newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's pension scheme faces critical vote.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's pension scheme faces critical vote.

text.p: Hong Kong's plan to set up a retirement fund with required employee and employer contributions may founder on Friday when legislators vote on whether to extend financing for the fund's working group.

Pamela Tan, director of the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) office, said on Thursday it is too early to tell if the funding request will be accepted, despite heavy lobbying of legislators by her office.
"We have worked very hard to lobby legislators, but it is still too early to predict a result," she said.
The MPF office is charged with recommending guidelines to balance the risks and returns of MPF investments.
The MPF as planned requires employees and employers to each contribute five percent of monthly salary to a retirement fund.
Opponents charge that workers' assets would be at risk because the funds would be managed by the private sector rather than by the government, and favour a government-managed system.

On January 29, a sub-committee of the Legislative Council's Finance Committee voted 11 to six to deny the MPF office HK$25 million, which would have kept it operational for the 13 months from March, allowing it to complete its work.
The full Finance Committee will vote on the MPF funding on Friday. If the group votes to withhold funding, the MPF office will shut down, effectively suspending the MPF plan.
Tan said the plan is flexible enough to address opponents' concerns, while a vote to suspend the office will destroy any chance of developing a pension scheme in the near term.
Since the vote by the sub-committee in January, the MPF office has made some concessions to soothe the opposition's concerns about the safety and fairness of the scheme.
